title: The disciples’ desire
summary: Jesus asks his disciples what they desire after he departs to the Father. Most ask to finish their ministry after living to the age of man and then come to him in his kingdom.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus asks each disciple what he desires after Jesus is gone to the Father.
All but three disciples ask to complete their ministry after living to the age of man and then come to Jesus in his kingdom.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus addresses the disciples assembled before him.
unspecified_visual_details: The disciples’ individual identities among the group and the exact setting are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: What is it that ye desire of me, after that I am gone to the Father?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

spoken_dialogue.text: We desire that after we have lived unto the age of man, that our ministry, wherein thou hast called us, may have an end, that we may speedily come unto thee in thy kingdom.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The twelve Nephite disciples

prohibited_inventions: Do not identify which disciples speak or which three abstain.

title: The first answer
summary: Jesus tells the disciples that after they are seventy-two years old they will come to him in his kingdom and find rest with him.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus blesses the disciples for their desire and says that after they are seventy-two years old they will come to him in his kingdom and find rest with him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus speaks to the disciples who made the request.
unspecified_visual_details: Gestures, facial expressions, and surroundings are not specified.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a future arrival in the kingdom as a present event.

title: Jesus turns to the three

explicit_facts.text: Jesus turns to the three and asks what they want him to do after he goes to the Father.
The three sorrow in their hearts and do not dare speak what they desire.

unspecified_visual_details: The three disciples' identities and visible expression of sorrow are not specified.

title: Promise to the three
summary: Jesus promises the three they will never taste or endure the pains of death; when he comes in glory they will be changed from mortality to immortality and blessed in his Father's kingdom.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus promises the three they will never taste death and will live to behold the Father's doings until all things are fulfilled.
Jesus says that when he comes in glory they will be changed from mortality to immortality and blessed in his Father's kingdom.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus continues speaking to the three.
unspecified_visual_details: The future change and coming in glory are promised events, not present visual action.

title: Their ministry and joy
summary: Jesus says the three will have no pain while dwelling in the flesh except sorrow for the world's sins, because they desire to bring souls to him. He promises fullness of joy and speaks of the Father and the Holy Ghost.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus says the three will have no pain in the flesh or sorrow except for the sins of the world, because they desire to bring souls to him.
Jesus promises them fullness of joy in his Father's kingdom and says they will be as he is.
Jesus says the Holy Ghost bears record of the Father and him, and that the Father gives the Holy Ghost to the children of men because of Jesus.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus speaks to the three disciples.
unspecified_visual_details: The Father and the Holy Ghost are mentioned but not described as visibly present.

title: Jesus departs

title: The three are caught up
summary: The heavens open, and the three are caught up into heaven, where they see and hear unspeakable things that they are forbidden and unable to utter. They cannot tell whether they are in or out of the body; it seems to them like a transfiguration.

explicit_facts.text: The heavens open and the three are caught up into heaven, where they see and hear unspeakable things.
They are forbidden to utter what they see and hear and are not given power to do so.
They cannot tell whether they are in or out of the body; it seems to them like a transfiguration that changes them from flesh to an immortal state so they can behold the things of God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The three are the disciples identified as those who are to tarry.
unspecified_visual_details: The unspeakable things they see and hear are not described; their visual appearance during this experience is unspecified.

narration.text: the heavens were opened,
they were caught up into heaven,
they could not tell;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Do not invent imagery for the unspeakable things or treat the uncertain bodily state as a described visible transformation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show specific heavenly beings, places, or events not described.

title: Mormon Recounts Their Ministry
summary: Mormon recounts that they ministered again on earth without sharing what they had heard and seen, because of a commandment given in heaven. He does not know whether they were mortal or immortal after their transfiguration. According to the record, they ministered to all the people, united believers with the church, and baptized them. Those baptized received the Holy Ghost.

explicit_facts.text: They ministered again on earth but did not minister of what they had heard and seen because of a commandment given in heaven.
Mormon does not know whether they were mortal or immortal from the day of their transfiguration.
According to the record, they ministered to all the people, united those who believed their preaching with the church, and baptized them; those baptized received the Holy Ghost.

reasonable_visual_inferences: An undated illustration of people listening or being baptized could accompany Mormon’s account without presenting it as a newly documented occasion.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise setting, the people’s identities, the baptism method, and any visible appearance of the Holy Ghost are unspecified.

narration.text: they did again minister upon the face of the earth;
And now, whether they were mortal or immortal, from the day of their transfiguration, I know not;
they did go forth upon the face of the land, and did minister unto all the people,
baptizing them, and as many as were baptized did receive the Holy Ghost.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The first-person “I” in the narration is Mormon, the abridger, not one of the three disciples.
Present the ministry as Mormon’s account rather than a newly specified occasion.
Their mortal or immortal state is unknown to Mormon.
prohibited_inventions: Do not alter the quotation to insert Mormon’s name into it.
Do not depict or disclose what they heard and saw in heaven.
Do not identify the land as the land of Nephi or depict all twelve disciples as present.
Do not invent a visible appearance for the Holy Ghost.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict all twelve disciples as prisoners.

unspecified_visual_details: The exact setting, depth, and manner of deliverance are unspecified.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an unstated divine figure or specific supernatural visual effect.

They were converted to the Lord and united to the church of Christ; the people of that generation were blessed.

Mormon says he has seen them and they have ministered to him.

title: Future ministry among the nations
summary: Mormon says the three will be among Gentiles and Jews unknown to them, and will minister to Israel's scattered tribes and all nations, bringing many souls to Jesus. He says they are as angels of God and may show themselves to people as they see fit when they pray to the Father in Jesus's name.

explicit_facts.text: The three will be among Gentiles and Jews, who will not know them.
When the Lord sees fit, the three will minister to scattered Israel and all nations, kindreds, tongues, and people, bringing many souls to Jesus.
They are as angels of God and, if they pray to the Father in Jesus's name, can show themselves to whom they choose.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The future statements can be conveyed as off-screen narration without depicting the future groups or actions.
unspecified_visual_details: No particular future ministry setting, people, or appearance of the three is described.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict named or specific Gentile, Jewish, or Israelite groups as a present-time scene.

title: Warning and witness
summary: Mormon foretells great works by the three before judgment, including among the Gentiles. He warns those who will not hearken to Jesus and those he sent, and asks whether people can escape the justice of God.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon says great and marvelous works will be wrought by the three before the judgment of Christ, including among the Gentiles.
Mormon says that having all scriptures about Christ's marvelous works would make these things known as things that must come.
Mormon warns those who do not hearken to Jesus and those he has chosen and sent, saying they will not receive him at the last day.
Mormon says it would be better for such people not to have been born and asks whether they can escape God's justice.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon's warnings may be narrated off-screen without depicting future judgment or the people addressed.
unspecified_visual_details: The future works, judgment, and people addressed are not shown as present events.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The judgment-seat and justice language is part of Mormon's warning, not a present visual event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Christ judging people or invent a specific audience for Mormon's warning.

title: Mormon learns of the change
summary: Mormon recalls not knowing whether the three were changed from mortality to immortality, then reports that the Lord made known a change to their bodies so they would not taste death, pain, or sorrow except for the world's sins. This change keeps Satan from tempting them and the powers of earth from holding them until Christ's judgment, when they will receive a greater change and dwell eternally in heaven.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon once did not know whether the three caught up into heaven had been changed from mortality to immortality.
After inquiring of the Lord, Mormon learns their bodies had to change or they must taste death.
A change was wrought upon their bodies so they would not taste death or suffer pain or sorrow except for the sins of the world.
The change was not equal to the change at the last day; it prevents Satan from having power to tempt them, sanctifies them in the flesh, and keeps the powers of earth from holding them.
They are to remain in this state until Christ's judgment day, when they receive a greater change, enter the Father's kingdom, and dwell eternally in heaven.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon is the narrator; the Lord's revelation and the described bodily change need not be shown as present visual events.
unspecified_visual_details: The way the Lord made this known and the visible appearance of the three's changed bodies are unspecified.

narration.text: I have inquired of the Lord,
there was a change wrought upon their bodies,
that Satan could have no power over them,
to dwell eternally in the heavens.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Mormon's description is retrospective teaching; do not merge the earlier heavenly event with the later account of his inquiry.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Satan or an unreported appearance of the Lord.
